findings.where: Article specimen: the subhead 'So, what are the key ‘chapter topics’?' compared with the article title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law' above it (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The subhead is set in a heavy, near-bold Newsreader, while the article title above it is regular. So the smaller, lower-ranked heading looks heavier and darker than the title it sits under. The weight is also not among the weights the type-pair tile declares for the face (330 for the line, 400 for text, 700 for the wordmark).
findings.who_objects: The founder and Angélique. This specimen shows how every article's subheads will look once Angélique adds them. A subhead that outweighs the page title gets the rank backwards, and it goes against the type tile a few screens above it.

findings.where: Article specimen title 'The World's Best…' (desktop and phone), and the type-pair tile's 'Mark's voice, from the first line…'
findings.fault: Straight typewriter apostrophes are used in the display title and the type-pair text. Everywhere else the page uses curly marks: ‘chapter topics’, the curly quotes in the article body, 'Mark’s line (enters)' and 'Mark’s own sentence' in the footer. At the title's display size the straight tick stands out, and the like marks are not treated alike.
findings.who_objects: Mark, a lawyer who writes for governments and development banks, and readers who expect a carefully set legal journal. A straight tick in a headline reads as unedited copy and undercuts the editorial care the page claims.

findings.where: Article specimen: the lecture row 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge / Lecture · 23 April 2026' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The row's title and date line start about 4 px in from the left edge shared by the article text, the dividers above and below the row, and the caption. The row's left edge breaks the column's one alignment by a small amount, so it looks like a slip rather than a deliberate indent.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who is judging the article specimen as the product. A small misalignment right under the clean article column makes the PDF list, the part the research calls the product, look less finished than the prose.

findings.where: Motion sketch: the preview frame of the opening (desktop and phone), compared with the first screen it stands for
findings.fault: The preview shows a different composition from the real first screen: a chest-up close crop of the face with no lectern, and the line in a regular weight rather than the hero's light weight. The first screen now shows the smaller figure at the lectern and the light line, so this preview no longer matches the opening it says it animates.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who judges the opening from this sketch. The founder would be signing off a motion and a composition that do not match the page the visitor gets.
